author: rdc-rfc1-author-a (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: sys_rst_q only feeds the asynchronous reset of a two-stage clk_dbg reset synchroniser. That is the normal way to hand a reset into another domain: assertion is asynchronous and release is resynchronised before the counter. The multicycle path between asynchronous clocks has no effect on the reset.

author_reading.rationale: The clk_sys reset flop drives the clk_dbg chain asynchronously, and the multicycle declaration relaxes that path across asynchronous clocks; the counter is diagnostic only.

labels.rationale: dbg_rst is reset from sys_rst_q, a single clk_sys flop with no synchroniser in its own domain. The clocks are declared asynchronous, so this is a reset generated in another domain. The two dbg_rst stages in clk_dbg reduce the metastability risk but do not make the cross-domain reset safe.
labels.suspected_flaw: The release of dbg_rst depends on the unsynchronised sys_rst_q output. Whether the two clk_dbg stages are enough is a judgement the RTL alone does not settle.

labels.rationale: The system flop feeds the raw end of a two-stage debug reset chain, whose final stage releases the counter. The multicycle exception names the two clocks, while the reset root is driven by the system flop.

settlement.rationale: B is right: the dbg_rst chain is a correct reset synchroniser, and its raw input may come from any domain. A (and the author) treat the clk_sys flop driving the chain's reset as a cross-domain generated reset, but no clk_dbg functional register is released by it. Note that RDC-007's written trigger has no exemption for a synchroniser chain's reset, so it may report this good case.
